newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan shares drop in minimal year-end demand.
newsitem.headline: Jordan shares drop in minimal year-end demand.

text.p: Stocks on the Amman exchange saw across-the-board declines on Saturday with minimal demand triggered by end-of-year accounts window dressing, dealers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.69 percent to 152.32 points in business worth around 1 million dinars ($1.4 million).

Three large bloc trades in leading bluechips Arab Bank, Housing Bank and Jordan Cement Factories dominated nearly half of turnover in otherwise lacklustre trade with minimal buying activity, dealers said.
One bloc sale of over 400 shares in market heavyweight Arab Bank helped drag the official index down. The stock shed 1.50 dinars to 251.50 dinars.
Brokers said brokers and some banks who allow clients some overdrawing in accounts were suspending payments for book-keeping purposes ahead of end-of-year balance sheet window dressing.
"There was minimal demand with reservations by banks and brokers to raise extend facilities of clients accounts to clear the books before end-of-year book-keeping," one broker said.
The top price gainer was Jordan International Trading Centre which rose 0.04 dinars to 0.75 dinars in end-of-year portfolio shuffling.
Overall 34 shares fell on Saturday. Ten rose and four traded but closed unchanged.
